name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+13, among the most Democratic House seats
Incumbent Grijalva holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge ($2.3M vs $224K)
Prediction markets price the Democratic win near 96%
No public general-election polling; low-contest attention
model.rationale: The district's 13-point Democratic lean, Grijalva's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing her win odds near 96% all point to a safe Democratic hold, with no polling or ratings suggesting otherwise.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or unusually depressed turnout could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 7th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward Democrats. Adelita Grijalva holds the seat as the incumbent and has raised roughly $2.3 million, while Republican Daniel Butierez has brought in about $224,000 and reported only around $11,000 in the bank. Outside spending has modestly favored Grijalva as well.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 96 percent, and no public general-election polls are available in this race. With the district's strong lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and no sign of a well-funded Republican operation, the forecast treats this as a Safe Democratic hold. The main uncertainty is turnout in a low-attention contest, not which party wins the seat.
